quiz.0.question: 'Toasted bread, brioche and biscuit' aromas indicate which production method?
quiz.0.options.1: Metodo Classico (secondary fermentation in bottle with extended lees contact)
quiz.0.explanation: Toasted bread, brioche and biscuit aromas ('autolytic' notes) are exclusively produced by extended contact with spent yeast (lees) in a sealed bottle — the signature of Metodo Classico.
quiz.1.question: 'Pure green apple and pear aromas, no toasted notes, a faint sweet edge' — what is this most likely?
quiz.1.options.1: Prosecco DOC/DOCG (Charmat method, minimal lees contact)
quiz.1.explanation: Prosecco (Charmat method, short lees contact) shows pure, simple fruit (green apple, pear, peach), no autolytic complexity and is usually off-dry — the most instantly recognisable Italian sparkling profile.
quiz.2.question: What structural characteristic does Trento DOC typically show that distinguishes it from Franciacorta?
quiz.2.options.1: Even higher natural acidity and a more linear, alpine mineral character — from high-altitude, cool Trentino
quiz.2.explanation: Trento DOC vineyards are higher-altitude and cooler than Franciacorta — producing sparkling wines with even crisper natural acidity, a pronounced alpine mineral freshness and perhaps slightly less richness.
quiz.3.question: Compared with French Champagne, Franciacorta's fruit character is typically?
quiz.3.options.1: More expressive, warmer and riper — Italian sunshine in a glass
quiz.3.explanation: Franciacorta, made in northern Italy's warmer summers, typically shows riper, more generous fruit (peach, nectarine, brioche) compared with Champagne's more restrained, brioche-and-green-apple profile.
